Model diagnostic plots

Source: R/appraise.R, R/gamm4-methods.R, R/gjrm-diagnostics.R, and 2 more
appraise.Rd

Model diagnostic plots

Usage

appraise(model, ...)

# S3 method for class 'gam'
appraise(
  model,
  method = NULL,
  use_worm = FALSE,
  n_uniform = 10,
  n_simulate = 50,
  seed = NULL,
  type = NULL,
  n_bins = c("sturges", "scott", "fd"),
  ncol = NULL,
  nrow = NULL,
  guides = "keep",
  level = 0.9,
  ci_col = "black",
  ci_alpha = 0.2,
  point_col = "grey20",
  point_alpha = 1,
  line_col = "red",
  by_family = NULL,
  rank = NULL,
  scalable = NULL,
  scalable_threshold = 10000L,
  qq_bins = 1000L,
  density_bins = c(50L, 50L),
  ppcheck = FALSE,
  n_ppc = 50,
  density_method = c("kde", "histogram"),
  bandwidth = NULL,
  conditioning = NULL,
  ppc_batch_size = 10L,
  ...,
  n_dharma = 250L
)

# S3 method for class 'lm'
appraise(model, ...)

# S3 method for class 'gamlss'
appraise(model, ..., type = "quantile", seed = NULL, conditioning = NULL)

# Default S3 method
appraise(
  model,
  ...,
  type = NULL,
  seed = NULL,
  conditioning = NULL,
  n_dharma = 250L
)

# S3 method for class 'gamm4'
appraise(model, conditioning = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'gjrm'
appraise(
  model,
  ...,
  type = "quantile",
  seed = NULL,
  conditioning = NULL,
  response = NULL,
  ppcheck = FALSE,
  by_family = NULL,
  n_dharma = 250L
)

# S3 method for class 'gamm'
appraise(model, conditioning = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'gratia_diagnostic_proxy'
appraise(model, type = "quantile", ...)

# S3 method for class 'lme'
appraise(model, conditioning = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'merMod'
appraise(model, conditioning = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'sdmTMB'
appraise(
  model,
  conditioning = NULL,
  component = "response",
  field_method = c("mle-mvn", "mle-eb", "mle-mvn-integrated"),
  ...
)

Arguments

model

a fitted model supported by diagnostic_support, including lm, glm, gam/bam, gamm/gamm4, glmmTMB, univariate GJRM and sdmTMB.

...

arguments passed to patchwork::wrap_plots().

method

character or NULL; how to calculate reference quantiles. Probability integral transform (PIT) and quantile residuals use fixed uniform and standard-normal references, respectively. For quantile residuals, "normal" also selects that fixed reference; other named methods require traditional residuals. For deviance, response and Pearson residuals:

  • "uniform" applies the fitted inverse cumulative distribution function (CDF) to randomised uniform quantiles and averages the resulting ordered residuals over n_uniform draws.

  • "simulate" generates n_simulate response data sets at the fitting covariates. Responses are generated together when needed to preserve dependence, and their ordered residuals supply reference values and bands.

  • "marginal" approximates the pooled distribution of individual residuals, without bands for dependence. This is selected for BAM GEE and PQL correlations that do not define a joint response distribution. Explicit joint simulation is unavailable in those cases.

  • "normal" uses a normal approximation fitted to the residual location and scale. For dependent responses it omits bands based on independence.

  • "direct" is deprecated in favour of "uniform".

For ordinary GAMs, NULL selects "simulate" for Tweedie and "uniform" otherwise. Missing inverse CDFs cause a switch to simulation; missing response generators can cause a switch to a normal approximation for independent responses. Dependent responses use joint simulation when available, or marginal checks otherwise. For grouped families, NULL selects simulation if every component has a generator, or inverse-CDF sampling with a message if every component has an inverse CDF. If neither is available, it gives an error; a normal approximation must be requested explicitly.

use_worm

logical; should a worm plot be drawn in place of the QQ plot?

n_uniform

numeric; number of inverse-CDF draws to average when method = "uniform".

n_simulate

numeric; number of data sets to simulate from the estimated model when using the simulation method (method = "simulate") for QQ plots.

seed

numeric; the random number seed to use for method = "simulate" and method = "uniform", and for randomised quantile residuals and posterior predictive draws.

type

character or NULL; residual type: "deviance", "response", "pearson", "pit", "quantile", "dharma", or "surrogate" (for ocat() or multinom() GAMs). NULL uses the model-specific default: deviance for ordinary lm/glm/GAM fits, and quantile for supported grouped families, GJRM, sdmTMB and full mixed-model checks. glmmTMB uses Pearson residuals conditionally and response residuals marginally. Extracted GAM components follow the ordinary GAM defaults. See diagnostic_support.

n_bins

character or numeric; either the number of bins or a string indicating how to calculate the number of bins.

ncol, nrow

numeric; the numbers of rows and columns over which to spread the plots.

guides

character; one of "keep" (the default), "collect", or "auto". Passed to patchwork::plot_layout()

level

numeric; the coverage level for QQ plot reference intervals. Must be strictly 0 < level < 1. Used for quantile reference bands and traditional method = "simulate" or "normal" bands. Also controls posterior predictive intervals for discrete responses with ppcheck = TRUE.

ci_alpha, ci_col

Deprecated; use gratia_theme_get() theme settings instead. Colour and transparency of QQ reference intervals, including bands for quantile residuals.

point_col, point_alpha

Deprecated; use gratia_theme_get() theme settings instead. Colour and transparency used to draw points in the plots. See graphics::par() section Color Specification. This is passed to the individual plotting functions, and therefore affects the points of all plots. Pooled grouped residual panels map component identity to colour instead of using the constant point_col.

line_col

Deprecated; use gratia_theme_get() theme settings instead. Colour specification for the 1:1 line in the QQ plot and the reference line in the residuals vs linear predictor plot. Also used for the observed distribution when ppcheck = TRUE.

by_family

logical or NULL; separate indexed grouped-family components into facets. The default pools quantile residuals with component colours and facets traditional residuals. TRUE and FALSE explicitly select the layout. In appraise(), observed-versus-fitted values always use component facets. Standalone observed_fitted_plot() facets by default and permits explicit pooling. Ignored for ordinary models.

rank

logical or NULL; use within-component ranks on the horizontal axis of residual-versus-predictor plots. The default ranks pooled grouped plots and retains original predictors in facets. TRUE or FALSE overrides this independently of the residual type and layout. Only finite observations included in each component determine its ranks; average ties are used.

scalable

Logical or NULL; NULL automatically uses scalable plots at or above scalable_threshold retained fitting observations. TRUE or FALSE forces scalable or original rendering.

scalable_threshold

Positive integer; automatic switching threshold.

qq_bins

Maximum number of QQ/worm points per family component, including endpoints.

density_bins

Positive integer or pair giving heatmap grid dimensions.

ppcheck

logical; replace the residual histogram with a posterior_predictive_plot()? Defaults to FALSE. Requires a model and family supported by that function. Replicated distributions use ci_col. Discrete posterior points and interval bars default to opacity 0.8, while continuous density curves use 0.2. Explicitly supplying ci_alpha overrides these defaults as well as the QQ reference interval opacity.

n_ppc

positive integer; number of posterior predictive data sets when ppcheck = TRUE. Independent of the QQ plot's n_simulate.

density_method

Conditional-density estimator: "kde" (the default) uses KernSmooth::bkde2D() with Gaussian kernels; "histogram" uses unsmoothed rectangular bins. Only affects the residual heatmap.

bandwidth

Optional pair of positive bandwidths for the predictor and residual axes, in their plotted units. NULL uses normal-reference bandwidths, adjusted for two dimensions, with a fallback for constant axes. Used only for density_method = "kde" and conditional density.

conditioning

character or NULL; "conditional" holds fitted random effects fixed, "marginal" averages over new effects, and "gam_component" uses the extracted GAM. Availability and defaults depend on the model; see diagnostic_support.

ppc_batch_size

positive integer; number of posterior predictive draws to process together for scalable plots. Changing the batch size does not change results for a fixed seed.

n_dharma

positive integer; number of response simulations for type = "dharma". This is separate from n_simulate, which controls traditional QQ reference calculations. Defaults to 250.

response

NULL uses all responses; a single integer selects one. For mgcv::gfam() models, the integer indexes the family list and selects observations assigned to that component, including when families repeat. For joint GJRM models, it selects a response in model order. Selection is independent of by_family.

component

character; for delta sdmTMB models, select the complete "response", occurrence ("binomial"), or "positive" component. Positive-component checks use only observations with positive responses.

field_method

how to treat fitted sdmTMB fields: hold one posterior draw fixed ("mle-mvn"), hold estimates fixed ("mle-eb"), or average over fitted-field uncertainty ("mle-mvn-integrated"). See quantile_residuals() and diagnostic_support.

Details

Use type = "dharma" for simulation-based PIT residuals calculated internally using gratia's response generators; no DHARMa or mgcViz dependency is needed. These residuals lie in [0, 1], including exact endpoints, and do not require a response CDF. n_dharma controls their simulation count. All residual panels share one calculated vector. QQ and worm plots require method = NULL and use uniform reference quantiles, with approximate pointwise bands for independent responses. Bands are omitted for dependent responses. Censored and multivariate outcomes are unsupported. See dharma_residuals() for the calculation.

Use type = "surrogate" for mgcv::ocat() and mgcv::multinom() GAMs. The former uses a scalar latent logistic residual; the latter retains all category utilities, including category 0, as separate panels with centred Gumbel references. QQ and worm plots require method = NULL. Each appraisal shares one residual draw across panels, with the same draw in ordinary and scalable displays. Multinomial residuals are plotted against their own category probabilities; observed-versus-fitted panels compare category indicators with those probabilities. Pointwise bands are calculated separately for each utility. See surrogate_residuals().

With type = NULL, ordinary lm/glm/GAM fits use deviance residuals. Models fitted with mgcv::gfam() use randomised quantile (Dunn–Smyth) residuals when every active component supplies a supported CDF and probability limits for discrete or censored observations. Otherwise, a message identifies unsupported components and all components use deviance residuals; requesting type = "quantile" explicitly is an error when any component is unsupported. Components never mix residual scales. Invalid encodings or numerical CDF failures are errors.

Quantile residuals use each component's fitted parameters, dispersion and weights, including binomial trial counts and Gaussian precision weights. Gamma (including precision weights), negative binomial, beta, scaled-t, Tweedie, inverse Gaussian, ordinal and zero-inflated Poisson components are supported. Unrecognised custom-family bounds remain unsupported. A custom CDF must also support the probabilities just below discrete values and at censoring limits. Replacements for recognised family CDFs must use the same arguments and probability conventions. Scalar uncensored cnorm(), clog() and cpois() components are supported; genuine censoring requires recoverable, aligned censoring bounds. Matrix censored responses rejected by gfam() and upstream fitting failures are not repaired.

Use response = NULL to check every grouped-family component or a single integer to select a component by its position in the mgcv::gfam() family list. Repeated families remain distinct. Selection filters fitting observations without refitting the model and retains original component labels. by_family independently controls the layout of the selected data. With an explicit seed, selected residuals match the corresponding rows of an all-component calculation whenever all components support that calculation.

by_family = NULL pools quantile residuals with colours identifying indexed family components, including repeated uses of the same family. Traditional residuals use component facets with free axes by default. The pooled residual-versus-predictor plot uses within-component predictor ranks: (rank(eta, ties.method = "average") - 0.5) / n, where n counts the finite observations included for that component; constants map to 0.5. Facets retain original linear predictors. Use rank to override this choice independently of residual type or layout. The links and original predictor values can have different meanings across components; ranks compare positions within components, not effects on a common response scale. Pooled histograms use common bin edges and component-specific densities.

Quantile QQ and worm plots compare to fixed standard-normal quantiles, with an identity line or zero line. Independent responses have exact pointwise reference bands for ordered residuals. For dependent responses, bands use simulations that preserve dependence when a joint generator is available; otherwise they are omitted with an explanation. Bands condition on fitted parameters, exclude estimation uncertainty and do not provide simultaneous coverage. References calculated from simulation ranks also use simulated bands; see diagnostic_support. Worm plots subtract the same theoretical quantiles from residuals and reference bands. appraise() computes one seeded residual vector shared by its residual panels and always separates observed-versus-fitted values by component, because response units differ. Standalone observed_fitted_plot() allows explicit pooling. Ordinal panels use expected category codes.

Scalable plots aggregate all observations before rendering. Residual heatmaps show conditional density; observed-versus-fitted heatmaps show counts. Point styling applies to QQ/worm points, and heatmap fill scales can be changed with ggplot scales. QQ references average draws as they are generated or compute exact pooled quantiles using temporary files above the configured memory threshold; see diagnostic_support. Supported univariate GJRM::gamlss models use quantile residuals by default.

If the response expectation does not exist, the observed-versus-fitted panel explains why it is unavailable. Other supported panels remain usable. Prepared diagnostic objects can be given a new conditioning or field choice; the model is prepared again so all panels use the requested choice.

Note

The wording used in mgcv::qq.gam() uses direct in reference to the simulated residuals method (method = "simulated"). To avoid confusion, method = "direct" is deprecated in favour of method = "uniform".

See also

The plots are produced by functions qq_plot(), residuals_linpred_plot(), residuals_hist_plot(), observed_fitted_plot(), and optionally posterior_predictive_plot().

gamm4_support

Examples

load_mgcv()
## simulate some data...
dat <- data_sim("eg1", n = 400, dist = "normal", scale = 2, seed = 2)
mod <- gam(y ~ s(x0) + s(x1) + s(x2) + s(x3), data = dat)
## run some basic model checks
appraise(mod) & ggplot2::theme(
  geom.gratia.diagnostic.point = ggplot2::element_geom(colour = "steelblue"),
  gratia.alpha.diagnostic.point = 0.4)

## replace the residual histogram with a posterior predictive check
appraise(mod, ppcheck = TRUE, n_ppc = 20, seed = 42)


## To change the theme for all panels use the & operator, for example to
## change the ggplot theme for all panels
library("ggplot2")
appraise(mod, seed = 42) & theme_minimal()


## Select a grouped-family component by its position in the family list
set.seed(53)
grouped <- data.frame(x = runif(160), family_id = rep(1:2, 80))
grouped$component <- factor(grouped$family_id)
grouped$y <- rnorm(160, sin(2 * pi * grouped$x), 0.4)
is_count <- grouped$family_id == 2L
grouped$y[is_count] <- rpois(sum(is_count), exp(grouped$x[is_count]))
grouped_fit <- gam(cbind(y, family_id) ~ component +
  s(x, by = component, k = 6), data = grouped,
  family = gfam(list(gaussian(), poisson())), method = "REML")
appraise(grouped_fit, response = 2, seed = 54)

## Layout remains a separate choice
qq_plot(grouped_fit, response = 2, by_family = TRUE, seed = 54)
